title: Hands Fold a Paper Sheet
tests: Tests coherent hand anatomy, hand-object contact and a completed paper-folding action in one text-generated shot.

faults.what: The clip contains audible speech, transcribed as “přineseš.”, despite the explicit request for no sound.
The paper becomes a narrow strip with angled ends rather than the simple rectangular result of folding a sheet in half; the sequence appears to include additional folding.

judge.summary: The clip shows realistic overhead paper handling and crease pressing, but the folding result is wrong and unwanted speech breaks the silence requirement.

must_haves.item: Both human hands and the entire blue sheet remain visible on a wooden table.
must_haves.why: Both hands and the paper remain within the frame in all supplied images, on a wooden tabletop.

must_haves.item: The hands visibly bring one half of the sheet over the other, producing a folded sheet rather than an abrupt object replacement.
must_haves.why: The sampled frames show different folded configurations but do not establish the motion of one half passing over the other or whether the transitions are continuous.

must_haves.item: The hands press along the resulting crease after folding.
must_haves.why: The hands visibly flatten the folded paper in the later frames.

must_haves.item: Hands remain anatomically plausible, without extra or fused fingers, and make convincing contact with the paper.
must_haves.why: The visible hands look anatomically plausible and rest naturally against the paper, with no clear extra or fused fingers.

must_haves.item: The blue paper remains a single consistent object throughout the action.
must_haves.why: The images consistently show one blue paper object, with no visible duplication or material change.

must_haves.item: The eight-second widescreen video uses one fixed overhead shot and has no sound.
must_haves.why: The supplied duration is eight seconds and the images show consistent widescreen overhead framing, but the sound report explicitly records speech.
